title: Enterprise Active Directory Health, Security and Recovery-Readiness Capstone
summary: Perform an evidence-first assessment of replication, DNS/DC Locator, FSMO/time, authentication, secure channels, delegation, privileged access, DC lifecycle and forest-recovery readiness, then produce a prioritized remediation and recovery plan.
scenario: You are the senior engineer taking ownership of a three-domain Active Directory forest with 14 domain controllers across datacenter and branch sites. The environment has intermittent replication alerts, inconsistent site/subnet documentation, legacy LDAP consumers, aging backups, one branch RODC, a planned Windows Server 2025 functional-level uplift, and an upcoming external forest trust. Leadership requires a defensible health, security and recovery-readiness decision before major change begins.
business_context: The forest supports business-critical authentication and infrastructure services. The organization has a four-hour standard maintenance window, an acquisition-related trust planned within six months, and audit pressure to demonstrate least privilege, recoverability and change evidence rather than informal administrative knowledge.
technical_constraints: No forest-wide outage is authorized for the assessment; all discovery must begin read-only; destructive recovery, metadata cleanup, trust reset or secure-channel repair requires a separately approved change or incident path; recovery testing must occur in isolation before production use.
functional_requirements: Build a per-DC replication health map from Repadmin and Directory Service evidence, including failure age and tombstone-lifetime risk.
Validate AD-integrated DNS/DC Locator and site/subnet alignment for representative datacenter and branch clients.
Inventory FSMO holders, Global Catalog placement and forest-root PDC emulator time-source health.
Classify member-computer secure-channel incidents separately from domain-controller trust problems and document the correct diagnostic tools for each.
Assess Group Policy/SYSVOL dependency risk, LDAP signing/channel-binding readiness and delegated OU administration against least-privilege principles.
Review branch RODC Password Replication Policy and privileged-credential exposure assumptions.
Verify trusted System State recovery points, DSRM/recovery credential readiness and the documented forest-recovery sequence in an isolated exercise.
Produce a Windows Server 2025 functional-level readiness decision based on actual DC versions, replication health, backup readiness and change prerequisites.
Produce a prioritized remediation backlog with evidence, owner, risk, maintenance-window requirement, validation and rollback/escalation boundary for every action.
non_functional_requirements: Assessment activity must not require a forest-wide outage.
Read-only evidence collection is the default; state-changing commands must be separated into approved remediation tasks.
Results must be understandable to senior infrastructure engineers, security stakeholders and non-technical leadership.
No finding may be marked closed without post-change or recovery validation evidence.
architecture_decisions: Treat replication, DNS, sites, time and authentication as one dependency graph during incident triage rather than as isolated products.
Treat Tier-0/privileged identity findings, unconstrained or weak delegation and legacy LDAP compatibility as security risks with explicit owners.
Use the latest trusted recovery point, not automatically the newest backup, and rehearse forest recovery on an isolated network.
Do not raise functional levels until all required DC-version and health prerequisites are evidenced.
Do not use metadata cleanup, secure-channel repair, trust reset or forced synchronization merely to clear symptoms; each requires a diagnosed failure mode and bounded change plan.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Evidence baseline: collect replication, Directory Service, DNS/DC Locator, site/subnet, FSMO/GC, time and authentication evidence without changing configuration.
Phase 2 - Security/control review: assess LDAP protections, OU delegation, privileged administration, gMSA, RODC password-replication policy and upcoming trust exposure.
Phase 3 - Recovery readiness: inventory trusted backups and recovery credentials, select recovery DCs per domain, rehearse the documented recovery flow in isolation, and record actual timing/issues.

Phase 4 - Remediation sequencing: rank findings by business impact, security exposure, replication age and recovery risk; fit safe changes into approved windows and isolate high-impact work into dedicated changes.
Phase 5 - Modernization gate: only after health/recovery closure, assess Windows Server 2025 DC/functional-level uplift and any legacy dependency remediation.
Phase 6 - Revalidation: rerun the evidence baseline and prove that each remediated risk is closed without creating new replication, authentication or policy regressions.
risk: The highest risks are uncontrolled privileged access, stale or nonconvergent directory data, untrusted recovery points, legacy LDAP dependencies, and introducing trust/functional-level changes before the forest is demonstrably healthy and recoverable.
security: Security findings must include privilege scope, exposed credentials or trust boundary, affected assets, evidence, compensating controls and a bounded remediation path. Recovery from suspected compromise must avoid reconnecting recovered DCs to potentially unsafe partners before the isolation and trust-reset plan is complete.
operations: Create a standing operations pack containing daily/weekly replication evidence, DNS/DC Locator checks, FSMO/GC/time inventory, privileged-group review cadence, backup/recovery-point status and escalation thresholds for stale DCs or trust failures.
cost: Prefer operational and configuration remediation using existing Windows Server capabilities. Any new monitoring, backup or privileged-access platform cost must be justified by a specific control gap rather than assumed as a capstone requirement.
validation: The capstone passes only when the learner produces traceable evidence for every DC and major dependency, a trusted recovery-point decision, an isolated recovery-drill result, a least-privilege/security gap register, and a prioritized remediation plan with explicit validation criteria.
rollback_dr: Every state-changing remediation must include a rollback or recovery boundary. Forest recovery remains a last-resort, incident-governed operation; secure-channel repair, trust reset, metadata cleanup and functional-level changes are never presented as casual troubleshooting steps.

assessment_rubric.evidence_quality: Every conclusion cites concrete diagnostic or configuration evidence rather than relying on a single forest-wide health statement.
assessment_rubric.dependency_reasoning: Replication, DNS, sites, time, Kerberos, secure channel and policy symptoms are correlated correctly before remediation is proposed.
assessment_rubric.security_judgement: Privileged access, LDAP, delegation, gMSA, RODC and trust findings are prioritized by blast radius and business context.
assessment_rubric.recovery_readiness: The plan identifies trusted backups, recovery DCs, isolation requirements, credentials and an exercised recovery sequence rather than saying only 'test DR'.
assessment_rubric.change_safety: Destructive or state-changing actions are isolated behind explicit approval, scope, rollback and validation gates.
assessment_rubric.modernization_readiness: Windows Server 2025/functional-level recommendations are conditional on proven prerequisites and legacy compatibility evidence.
assessment_rubric.executive_communication: The final report expresses technical findings as business risk, priority, owner and measurable closure criteria.
